candidates.title: Good Days Are Easy
candidates.why_people_may_share: The send-trigger is immediate: someone sends this when they want to say, 'I don't just want you when things are easy.'
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Warm comments like 'bad days do', 'this is us', and tagging the person who stayed through a rough patch.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Soft chest-hit for couples who have survived anxiety, distance, fights, or low weeks without making it dramatic.

candidates.title: When I'm Not Easy
candidates.suggested_text_hook: Promise you'll stay when I'm not easy to love.
candidates.why_people_may_share: This gives the sender a vulnerable line without sounding needy.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Confession-style comments: 'this one hurt', 'needed this', 'he really did'.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Tender recognition with a little ache.

candidates.title: No Big Speech
candidates.suggested_text_hook: I don't need a big promise.
candidates.why_people_may_share: For couples whose love language is presence, not speeches.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Comments like 'bare minimum but rare' or tagging the partner who quietly shows up.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Gentle, saveable, less dramatic than the others.

top_pick.title: Good Days Are Easy
top_pick.reason: Strongest 3-second hook and cleanest swipe logic, but it changes the requested source text.

engagement_rationale.send_trigger: It lets someone ask for steadiness without writing a paragraph.
engagement_rationale.tag_reason: They tag the partner who stayed during a bad day.
engagement_rationale.comment_bait: Bad days do; this is us; you did stay.

distribution_risks: If the art is only hands with no Aachu/Zuv specificity, it may feel like a generic couple quote.
The word promise can become greeting-card-soft unless the bad-day line stays sharp.
Avoid captioning it with true-love language; the post already earns the emotion.
